learned counsel for the appellant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the entire record.
In view of the order which is proposed to be passed today, notice to opposite party No.2 is dispensed with.

The instant criminal appeal has been filed by the appellant against the judgment and order dated 18.10.2024 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge/F.T.C. 1st, District Ayodhya in Sessions Trial No.144 of 2024 (State vs. Amar) arising out of Case Crime No.68 of 2024, under Sections 376 and 506 I.P.C. relating to Police Station Raunahi, District Ayodhya, whereby the learned trial Court has rejected the application for declaring the appellant juvenile vide order dated 14.08.2024.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the impugned order passed by the learned trial Court is patently illegal whereby the application moved by the appellant to the effect that he was juvenile on the date of alleged incident on the basis of his date of birth as recorded in the High School Certificate, has been rejected.

The said fact has not been disputed by the learned A.G.A.
His further submission is that once such an application was moved by the appellant claiming himself to be a juvenile on the date of alleged incident, it was incumbent upon the learned trial Court to have proceeded to dispose of the same in strict accordance with the provisions contained in Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (hereinafter referred to as "J J Act").

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: However, this was was not done by the learned trial Court before rejecting the application seeking a determination of juvenility by means of the impugned order dated 18.10.2024.
His next submission is that in the aforesaid view of the matter, the impugned order dated 18.10.2024 being unsustainable in law deserves to be set aside.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the aforesaid prayer.
However, he has been unable to dispute the legal submissions advanced by learned counsel for the appellant.

Having heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned A.G.A. for the State and upon perusal of the record, it transpires that the appellant has been convicted for the offence under Sections 376 and 506 I.P.C. in Sessions Trial No.144 of 2024 (State vs. Amar) arising out of Case Crime No.68 of 2024.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An application came to be moved on behalf of the present appellant claiming himself to be a juvenile on the date of alleged incident on the basis of his death of birth as recorded in the High School Certificate.

Thus, in the aforesaid undisputed factual background, it was incumbent upon the learned trial Court to proceed to determine the juvenility of the appellant in strict accordance with the provisions contained in J J Act itself after affording an opportunity of hearing to the victim/ first informant/
complainant of the case concerned and to the State also.
However, it does not appear from the impugned order that the learned trial Court has followed the aforesaid procedure.

It is needles to mention that the learned trial Court was also required to record a finding of fact on the basis of material available before it as to whether the present appellant was juvenile on the date of alleged incident or not.
However, the same was required to be done in strict accordance with the provisions contained in J J Act.

A bare perusal of the impugned order does not reflect that while passing the impugned order,
learned trial Court has followed the procedure prescribed in J J Act in this regard.

Therefore, in the considered opinion of this Court, the impugned order dated 18.10.2024 is not sustainable in law,
which deserves to be set aside and is accordingly set aside.

The matter is remanded back to the learned court below to pass an order afresh on the application moved on behalf of the appellant claiming juvenility with utmost expedition by means of a speaking and reasoned order in strict accordance with law.
